keyVerseText: Which came with Zerubbabel: Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel: Seraiah: also called, Azariah, nehe.7.7.
rootMeaning: The root of רְעֵלָיָה (Reelaiah) derives from רָעַל (râʻal), meaning to shake or reel, combined with יָהּ, a shortened form of the divine name Yahweh. This etymology suggests the meaning 'made to tremble before Yahweh' or 'bearer of Jehovah,' emphasizing a trembling or reverent fear inspired by God. The literal sense conveys a dynamic image of one who is deeply affected or moved by the presence and power of God, beyond a mere proper name.
usageInScripture: The word רְעֵלָיָה appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Ezra 2:2, where it is used as a proper name, Reelaiah, referring to an Israelite who returned from exile with Zerubbabel. It is consistently translated as 'Reelaiah' and is identified as a masculine personal name linked to the post-exilic community. The limited occurrence underscores its function as a distinctive identity marker rather than a common noun, highlighting the faithfulness of those who returned to Jerusalem.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding רְעֵלָיָה as 'bearer of Jehovah' rooted in trembling before God enriches our appreciation of the biblical narrative of restoration and covenant faithfulness. This name reflects the deep reverence and dependence on God that characterized the returned exiles, reminding believers that true restoration involves a heart responsive to God's sovereign presence. It also points forward to the Christian call to live in awe of God, whose power and holiness inspire both reverence and trust. Theologically, it signifies that God's people are defined not only by their heritage but by their posture before Him—one of trembling faithfulness empowered by the Lord.
keyVerseReflection: Ezra 2:2 lists Reelaiah among those who returned with Zerubbabel, emphasizing the community of faith that rebuilt Jerusalem after exile. The inclusion of Reelaiah, whose name means 'bearer of Jehovah,' highlights the spiritual identity of the returnees as those who carry God's presence with them. This verse thus not only records a historical fact but also symbolizes the gathering of a people renewed in their commitment to God, underscoring the importance of reverence and divine empowerment in the restoration process.
